about: Real reviewer candidates, copied verbatim from two end-to-end runs of the PR review cycle (PR 205: two reviewers; PR 207: two reviewers and two further probe reviewers), as each reviewer reported them. Ids are the reviewer prefix and the reviewer's own slug. Used by pr-review-ledger-resemblance.test.js: the words a finding is compared on depend on the whole round, so each round is kept whole.

pr207.failureMode: The command's Phase 4 landing silently writes the AC's test into the collection-definition class. That class has no fixture constructor, so any body using `_fixture` (the shape the PR mandates for xUnit) fails to compile, the real spec class never gets the test, and the project's collection definition is mutated. Hits every consumer whose xUnit E2E project keeps its CollectionDefinition beside the tests — the same 'sibling spec class' the PR tells the orchestrator to copy `collection`/`fixtureType` from.

pr207.failureMode: Whenever detection is ambiguous (mixed-framework dir, CPM/shared-props csproj, transitive test SDK) the orchestrator converts 'unknown' into an assertion of 'nunit'. Appending to an existing xUnit spec then hard-throws instead of inferring from the file, and a new file is scaffolded as NUnit into an xUnit project. Passing undefined on null would preserve the safety net the module was built with.

Verified: appendTestMethod(xunitFile, {framework:'nunit', ...}) throws "framework mismatch: the existing file uses xunit but framework 'nunit' was requested."

pr207.failureMode: A consuming project that uses Playwright's own xUnit bindings (`Microsoft.Playwright.Xunit`, or `xunit` + a `PageTest`-derived base class) is detected as framework 'xunit' and is then routed into the ONLY xUnit shape the writer knows: a `[Collection]` class with a fixture injected through the constructor. `scaffoldNewSpecFile` ignores `baseClass` entirely for xunit (`if (framework === 'nunit') assertBaseClass(baseClass)`, spec-writer.js:188) and `scaffoldXunitFile` hard-throws without `collection`/`fixtureType` (spec-writer.js:217-224) — a Playwright.Xunit project has neither, so the landing step cannot write the file at all. The agent is also told something false for that project: "framework 'xunit' means no PageTest `Page`: build the context and page as the project's sibling tests do" (agents/playwright-tester.yaml:61) — Microsoft.Playwright.Xunit does provide `PageTest`/`Page`. The detector cannot distinguish the two xUnit worlds the feature actually cares about (core Microsoft.Playwright + own fixture vs. the Playwright xUnit bindings), yet the CHANGELOG scopes support to only the first.
pr207.evidence: e2e-framework.js:25 `if (name.startsWith('xunit') || name === 'microsoft.playwright.xunit') xunit = true;` and tests/e2e-framework.test.js asserts `Microsoft.Playwright.Xunit` -> 'xunit'. spec-writer.js:188 skips the base-class check for xunit and spec-writer.js:193 unconditionally dispatches to scaffoldXunitFile, which throws `collection must be the project's xUnit collection name ... copy it from a sibling spec class.` Root CHANGELOG line scopes support to "xUnit projects that build their own page per test (core `Microsoft.Playwright` with a `[Collection]` fixture)". Playwright .NET docs show the xUnit bindings shape (`using Microsoft.Playwright.Xunit; public class Tests : PageTest { [Fact] ... Page ... }`): https://playwright.dev/dotnet/docs/test-runners and https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/main/docs/src/writing-tests-csharp.md

pr207.failureMode: Only the Proposal request gained `framework`; the Run request shape, the Run-stage agent responsibility and the Phase 4 step 2 action are unchanged. The Run stage is explicitly a fresh, stateless invocation ("no memory of the Proposal stage"), so the running agent has no way to know the project builds its own browser/context. Mode and slowMo are delivered as Playwright *launch* options — the agent is told to prefer `dotnet test -- Playwright.LaunchOptions.SlowMo=<ms>` (agents/playwright-tester.yaml:79-80) and `resolveRunConfig` returns `{headless, slowMo}` — but those runsettings-level options are honoured only by the Playwright .NET test bindings' base classes, not by a hand-rolled `[Collection]` fixture that calls `LaunchAsync` with its own options. For exactly the xUnit shape this PR adds, REQ-013's once-per-session headed/headless choice and the follow-along pause silently do nothing, and nothing in the new wiring tells the agent or the QA engineer that.

pr207.failureMode: For a new xUnit spec file the writer requires `collection` and `fixtureType` "copied from a sibling spec class", but (a) nothing in the workflow collects them — Phase 2 step 4 only resolves `framework`, and no step reads a sibling class, and (b) an xUnit E2E project with no sibling spec yet (the first test, the same situation the command handles for EvidenceCapture.cs by generating the helper) has nothing to copy. The throw then happens at Phase 4 step 3, i.e. after the AC was authored, presented, accepted and actually run against the QA environment, and that step has no failure branch (unlike the Proposal stage's markManual escape hatch), so the session has nowhere to go. The same gap applies to `testBody`: xunit now hard-requires it, and the workflow never says how `proposedTest` is reduced to a method body.

The contract the command was given covers only the null case — 'carry the result forward as framework ("nunit" when it returns null)' — so an unexpected throw aborts Phase 2 instead of falling back to the documented NUnit default. (Symlinked project directories are also silently skipped, since `entry.isDirectory()` is false for a symlink.)

Every sibling input the PR added is strictly guarded against exactly that — `collection` via COLLECTION_NAME_RE, `fixtureType`/`usings` via DOTTED_IDENTIFIER_RE — and the new test suite even exercises the attack shape `collection: 'X") ] class Y {'`. The behaviour is pre-existing (the module header already hedges "a C# NUnit/MSTest bracket attribute"), but this PR now locks it in with a byte-exact GOLDEN assertion, which makes the wrong attribute harder to fix later and sits oddly beside the framework-fidelity goal.

pr207.failureMode: detectE2eFrameworkInDir only reads `<PackageReference Include="...">` out of `.csproj` files, and the command's documented fallback for null is "nunit". Common real xUnit layouts therefore detect as null: test packages declared in a shared Directory.Build.props/Directory.Packages.props (the E2E csproj then only references Microsoft.Playwright), `<Using Include="Xunit" />` implicit-usings style, single-quoted MSBuild attributes, or any tree that also holds an NUnit unit-test project (both -> ambiguous -> null). The consumer then gets a brand-new spec file scaffolded as NUnit (`using Microsoft.Playwright.NUnit; [TestFixture] ... : PageTest` with `[Test]`) wrapping an xUnit `_fixture`-based body - a file that cannot compile - with no warning. The append path is protected by inferFramework, but the scaffold path has no equivalent safety net (it could infer from a sibling spec `.cs`, which the command already tells the orchestrator to read for collection/fixtureType, or treat null as stop-and-ask instead of silently NUnit).
pr207.evidence: Probe p1: detectE2eFramework('<PackageReference Include="Microsoft.Playwright" .../>') -> null; Include='xunit' (single quotes) -> null; '<Using Include="Xunit" />' + Microsoft.Playwright -> null; dir containing an xunit E2E csproj plus an NUnit unit-test csproj -> null. Probe p2: scaffoldNewSpecFile({framework:'nunit', ...xUnit body}) emitted `public class DashboardE2ETests : PageTest` / `[Test]` around `_fixture.CreateBrowserContext()`.

pr207.failureMode: appendTestMethod inserts before the closing brace of the FIRST `class ... {` in the file (findClassBodyRange:381). xUnit's canonical layout, which this PR now generates against (`[Collection("X")]` + a `[CollectionDefinition("X")] class ... : ICollectionFixture<...>` marker class), routinely puts a non-test class first in the same file. The confirmed, already-passed `[Fact]` is then written into the collection-definition (or fixture) class: the AC gets no runnable test and the file stops compiling (`_fixture` is not in scope there). The first-class-wins rule predates this PR, but NUnit's one-`[TestFixture]`-per-file shape rarely hit it; the xUnit shape introduced here makes it a normal case, and neither the new code nor the new command text picks the class carrying `[Collection]`/existing `[Fact]` members.
pr207.evidence: Probe p5: appendTestMethod on a file with `[CollectionDefinition("PlaywrightCollection")] public class PlaywrightCollection : ICollectionFixture<PlaywrightAppFixture> { }` above `[Collection("PlaywrightCollection")] public class SmokeE2ETests` put the new `[Fact] Dashboard_Renders` inside PlaywrightCollection, leaving SmokeE2ETests untouched.

pr207.failureMode: validateProposalRequest validates `framework`, but validateProposalResponse never reads `req.framework`: nothing rejects a proposal whose body uses NUnit's PageTest `Page` when framework === 'xunit' (or `_fixture`/`context.NewPageAsync()` when framework === 'nunit'). The hint is prose-only for the agent, so a stage that ignores it produces a body spec-writer happily wraps in the other framework's class, and the mismatch only surfaces as a C# compile error in the consumer's repo. This is weaker than the sibling evidence requirement in the same function, which is enforced through hasEvidenceCapture - the same style of check (e.g. reject `Page.` for xunit, reject `_fixture`/`NewPageAsync` for nunit) is available here.

The orchestrator is told only to 'copy them from a sibling spec class' in prose, with no helper and no validation step, so on an xUnit project with no sibling spec (the first AC of a fresh suite) the throw lands in Phase 4 landing - after the QA engineer confirmed the test and after the run passed, wasting the human gate. Detecting collection/fixtureType alongside the framework (both come from the same sibling spec) or carrying them in the proposal response would close it.

pr207.failureMode: The inference regexes require `]` or `(` immediately after the attribute name, so the common combined-attribute style `[Fact, Trait("Category","E2E")]` / `[Test, Category("E2E")]` is not recognised. In a project with global/implicit usings (the .NET 6+ test template default) such a file infers null, so the new mismatch guard silently no-ops and an append with no framework writes an NUnit `[Test]` + `await Page.GotoAsync(TestConfiguration.QaBaseUrl)` method into a real xUnit class. Separately, `[Theory]` is also an NUnit attribute, so an NUnit file whose only marker is `[Theory]` infers 'xunit'.
